orleanscathedral.name: Orléans Cathedral
orleanscathedral.slogan: Twin towers that watched over Joan's city for centuries.
orleanscathedral.line: Begun in 1601 under Henri IV, with Marie de' Medici laying the first stone, it was only consecrated in 1829.

maisonjeannedarc.name: Maison de Jeanne d'Arc
maisonjeannedarc.slogan: The timbered house where the Maid slept during the siege.
maisonjeannedarc.line: Joan lodged here with treasurer Jacques Boucher in spring 1429; the house was destroyed in 1940 and rebuilt in 1965.

sullychateau.name: Château de Sully-sur-Loire
sullychateau.slogan: Moat, keep and a king's minister on the Loire.
sullychateau.line: Voltaire, exiled from Paris, took refuge in this château in 1716 and again in 1719.

saintbenoitabbey.name: Fleury Abbey
saintbenoitabbey.slogan: Fifty columns hold up a porch, and a saint rests below.
saintbenoitabbey.line: Founded around 640, it is reputed to hold the relics of St Benedict, and its great tower porch stands on fifty columns.

briarepontcanal.name: Briare Canal Bridge
briarepontcanal.slogan: Boats sail 662 metres across the Loire on a river of steel.
briarepontcanal.line: Opened in 1896, it was the longest navigable aqueduct in the world until Magdeburg's in 2003.
